paragraphs: Rav Bibi bar Avin, in Yochanan’s name. Ze'ira: “Rav Bibi won this teaching: I and he sat before Rabbi Yochanan when he said this teaching, and he preceded me and reported it.” See Navla, where the reading differs. Niddah 25b has bar Abaye. Yuchasin rightly prefers bar Avin: Abaye, Bibi’s father, was much later than Yochanan; this is straightforward. The new Talmud editions did not correct it. Bibi bar Avin from Amram from Yitzchak from Yochanan, all supposedly contemporaries. (I did not find it; perhaps Idi bar Avin: Amram lived with Abaye and Rava.) This Bibi was in the Land when Zeira ascended before him. Bibi spoke to Rabbi—requires examination—and Assi in the West. Zeira: “By master’s life, I, Rav Assi, and Chiyya bar Abba.” Megillah Midrash, “White, fine linen”: Bibi bar Avina.
